title: I tested my AI game framework with a simple clone. Now I’m building the real game or maybe We!
author: WolrdInDust
selftext:
https://reddit.com/link/1tztxqr/video/zgo9msumny5h1/player

A while ago I made a small browser game called Chain. Honestly, the first version was very Flappy-like and I knew that. It was never meant to be the final “original game”. I used it mostly to test a bigger idea I had been thinking about for a while: what if beating a game could let you add the next playable part of it?

That idea became something I’m calling the IdeaChain Model. The simple version is: a player completes a challenge, gets a creation slot, describes what should come next, and the system tries to turn that idea into playable content after validation. So instead of only getting a score, a leaderboard position, or a skin, the player can leave something behind inside the game.

The first Chain prototype helped me learn something useful. Some people saw the chain idea and thought it was interesting. Some people mostly saw “Flappy clone”, and honestly, fair. That made it clear to me that the concept might be worth exploring, but it needs a more original game around it if I want to prove the model properly.

So now I’m working on a new version called Orbit Chain. It is still simple and one-tap, because I like the idea of games that anyone can understand quickly, but the mechanic is different. You launch between anchors, avoid hazards, escape the rising Void, reach the Gate, and eventually describe the next world. The important part is still the same: if you win, you can add what comes next.

I do not want this to be “prompt → random live level”, because that would break immediately. People would create broken levels, impossible levels, boring levels, NSFW stuff, exploits, or just abuse the system for fun. The version I’m trying to build is more like: player idea → structured blueprint → controlled game components → validation → playable content. So the player gets authorship, but not unlimited control.

I’m also planning to publish the IdeaChain Model on GitHub with the core principles, examples, schemas, validation notes, and implementation ideas. Not because I think I already solved it, but because I think this kind of model only gets better if people can criticize it, fork it, and try different versions of it. It could work in many genres: a tower game where winners add the next floor, a boss game where winners describe the next boss, a puzzle game where winners add the next room, or an arcade game where winners create the next world.

The thing I’m trying to prove is pretty simple: games can grow through the people who complete them. The winner does not just finish the game. The winner helps extend it.

Current demo:  
[https://worldclaimed.com/orbit-chain](https://worldclaimed.com/orbit-chain)

Would love honest feedback! Does “beating the game lets you add what comes next” feel like a strong loop? What genre would fit this best? And how would you validate player-described content before letting it become part of a live game?

comments.author: Ill-Past4609
comments.body: Nice!  What engine did the u use? And most important how did you get the spinning planet animation? The planets that have the aura around them ? That look like a black hole

replies.author: WolrdInDust
replies.body: Thanks! Custom TS/React + Canvas 2D, no full engine. The spin/aura is procedural: rotating sprites/rings, gradients, glow, and dust particles drawn every frame with request Animation Frame. The black-hole look is a separate visual layer over the gameplay gravity field.

replies.author: Ill-Past4609
replies.body: Ahh nice!! Looks clean! Very nice 😊 currently stuck with animations in Godot still haven’t figured out how to do it even manually

comments.author: HealthyWest6482
comments.body: i think the idea is novel. can't be the only thing going for it, has to genuinely be cool without etc.  could be clean if the authoring part is done inline through gesture (their last successful move being a creation move?) rather a detached system to 'add this thing with this hazard'. the merging of the gimmick + gameplay would feel most natural. seasons/ladders/challenges +1 i think.

replies.author: WolrdInDust
replies.body:
Yeah, I agree. The IdeaChain layer can’t carry the game by itself — the core gameplay still has to be fun without the explanation.

I really like your point about making the authoring feel more inline. For Orbit Chain, maybe the player’s last successful move / final path to the Gate could become part of the seed for the next world, instead of creation being only a separate form after the run.

Something like: “this is the move that won the Chain — now describe what kind of world should grow from it.”

Seasons, ladders and challenge-based chains also make a lot of sense. Thanks, this is very useful feedback.
